$comment: The telemetry a Semiont SDK's transports export over OTLP, in any language, when the process they run in exports at all: every span and metric, the transport it comes from, its kind, and the attributes it carries. `transport` is `bus` (the stream and emits) or `content` (uploads and reads). The SDK conformance suite holds each SDK to this table from outside: every row must arrive from its driver, of the listed kind, with every attribute not marked `only`, and whatever arrives under a row's name must carry only that row's attributes. A service that reaches the bus through an SDK exports these rows too; specs/src/service-telemetry/telemetry.json names such services under `sdk`, and their suites hold them to both tables. `semiont.bus.sent` counts the emits a client sent; the emits a gateway accepted are `semiont.bus.emit`, a row of that table, so that neither is counted as the other and the difference between them shows. In a span name, `{channel}` is the bus channel. Span kinds are OTLP's; a metric's `instrument` is `counter` (a monotonic sum).

spans.name: bus.emit:{channel}
spans.meaning: A frame the client sent, in the trace of the work that sent it.

attributes.only: on a frame in a resource scope

spans.name: bus.recv:{channel}
spans.meaning: A frame the client received, and the work done for it, in the trace the frame was sent under.

attributes.only: on a frame in a resource scope

spans.name: content.get
spans.meaning: A read of a resource's bytes.

attributes.only: on a read taken as a stream

spans.name: content.get_graph
spans.meaning: A read of a resource's description.

attributes.only: on an emit in a resource scope
